newsitem.title: USA: ATHLETICS-SLANEY AND NEARLY 60 OLYMPIANS WILL BE AT MILLROSE.
newsitem.headline: ATHLETICS-SLANEY AND NEARLY 60 OLYMPIANS WILL BE AT MILLROSE.

text.p: Nearly 60 international Olympians and the return of Mary Decker Slaney to the Millrose Games will highlight the 90th running of America's premier indoor track meet Friday at Madison Square Garden.
But there will be no Jackie Joyner-Kersee or Gail Devers as both Olympic champions pulled out Wednesday in a dispute over appearance fees, according to meet director Howards Schmertz.

Joyner-Kersee had been scheduled to race in the 60-metre hurdles in the first track appearance for the six-time Olympic gold medallist since last year's Atlanta Games. Devers had been expected to resume her duel with defending champion Gwen Torrence in the 60 metres.
Slaney, 38-year-old holder of 11 indoor and outdoor U.S. records ranging from 800 metres to 3,000 metres, will be at the event for the first time since finishing second in the mile in 1989.

Since then, she had been hobbled by a series of leg and ankle injuries. But even when she was not running, Slaney never gave up hope of racing again at Millrose where she had won the mile three times.
"Over the last few years when I have been hurt, inujured, sick, I thought that if I ever got healthy enough that I could run at least one indoor race, it would be Millrose," Slaney said.

A strong field of milers featuring defending Millrose champion Kathy Franey and 1995 champion Angela Chalmers of Canada will test Slaney around the 11-lap banked track. However, 1992 Olympic 1,500 metre champion Hassiba Boulmerka of Algeria withdrew after injuring an Achilles' tendon while training in Cuba earlier in the week, Schmertz said.
Slaney welcomed the challenge of an elite field.
"I would not have come if I didn't feel like I would be in good shape and very, very, very competitive," Slaney said. "I couldn't be happier."
Happiness is simply running at the Millrose Games for five-time Wanamaker Mile winner Marcus O'Sullivan, who will be competing in his 15th Millrose Games.

"Millrose is just not track and field, it's the tradition" said O'Sullivan, who finished second last year to Irish countryman Niall Burton. "Millrose will always be around and this is like running in my backyard."

Burton will be back to defend his crown in the marquee race against a strong international field that also includes Stephen Kipkorir of Kenya, Spainard Issav Viciosa and Paul McMullen of the United States.
Allen Johnson will stride to the starting line of the 60-metre hurldes looking to add the American indoor mark to his 110-metre hurdle Olympic record he set last year.
"I'm training to try to break the American record in the 60-metre hurdles this indoor season," Johnson said of Greg Foster's mark of 7.36.
An accomplished field including two-time Olympic champion Roger Kingdom, defending Millrose champion Courtney Hawkins and 1996 Olympic decathlon champion Dan O'Brien could challenge Johnson.
"I'm ready to run against anybody who shows up," said Johnson.
Last year Johnson lost the lead and a shoe when he clipped the fourth hurdle.
"It is always important to win. I feel it is important for me to win to get the season off on the right note," Johnson said. "This time my shoes will stay on."
